sources.title: Separate ministry announcements
sources.text: The Interior Ministry announced a port safety inspection. Separately, the Health Ministry denied reports that the central hospital would close. The two announcements concern separate decisions.

sources.title: Conditional electricity timetable
sources.text: The electricity utility plans to restore supply for up to six hours daily from November 2, subject to receiving fuel. Its director said the schedule is not guaranteed.

sources.title: Bank rejects withdrawal freeze claim
sources.text: Cedar Bank denied freezing customer withdrawals. Regulators said they are reviewing the bank but have not concluded that it is insolvent.

sources.title: Road reopening update
sources.text: The mountain road reopened at 09:00 UTC on October 23 after repairs. Heavy trucks remain prohibited. The road had closed on October 22.

sources.title: Economists issue forecast
sources.text: A university research team forecasts that food prices could increase by up to 8% next year. This is a forecast, not an observed increase. The estimate excludes energy prices.

sources.title: Permit article updated
sources.text: Updated October 23. The council approved the bridge permit on October 19. Construction has not begun. No opening date has been announced.

sources.title: Another outlet confirms earlier closure
sources.text: A second outlet confirms that the mountain road closed on October 22. This report adds no new information about the closure or repair timetable.

sources.title: Agency corrects inspection total
sources.text: The agency corrected its earlier report of 30 inspected buildings to 13. The earlier number was a transcription error, not a new inspection campaign.

sources.title: Weekend travel package
sources.text: A tour operator advertises a discounted weekend holiday package with a sponsored hotel promotion. No change in public services, safety or policy is reported.
